result:
Debater A's C₅ blow-up is valid. If each part carries a sparse triangle-free graph with independence number o(n), then α = o(n) and K₅-freeness hold, and the construction gives c ≥ 1/25. That bound does not rule out 1/8, so the question is whether a denser weighted triangle-free reduced graph beats C₅.

A's Step 3 is exactly that question, and A admits it was settled only by checking candidate graphs. Non-uniform weights on C₅, other odd-cycle blow-ups, and Andrásfai-type graphs are not ruled out. So A's upper bound of 1/25 is unproven.

I can prove one bound. Ramsey–Turán gives e(G) ≤ n²/4 + o(n²), so deleting at most e/2 edges for a max cut yields c ≤ 1/8. My earlier T₄(n) example fails the α = o(n) hypothesis, and I have no valid construction forcing n²/8 deletions. I therefore cannot defend 1/8 as the exact value on current evidence. But A cannot establish 1/25 either. The judge should not award either value as the exact answer without a proof of the upper bound for the weighted triangle-free problem.
